original: - TCA Cycle Intermediates (Malic & Citric Acid): Organic acids like malate and citrate feed directly into the exact same mitochondrial energy pathways as glutamine. Consuming clean, sour profiles—such as organic malic acid, tart cherries, or green apples—provides rapid, alternative fuel to gut epithelial cells, accelerating mucosal healing from a different biochemical angle.
rewrite: - TCA cycle intermediates are another quick fuel for the cells lining your gut, in both intestines. The TCA cycle is just another name for the citric acid cycle that glutamine feeds, and its intermediates are the compounds the cycle goes through as it makes energy. Malic acid and citric acid are two of them. They're also what makes some foods sour, so clean sour stuff like tart cherries, green apples or organic malic acid (you can buy it as a supplement) gives your gut cells a direct supply. Since those acids are already part of the cycle, they don't have to be turned into anything first, the way glutamine is turned into α-KG. They go directly into the same energy pathway in the mitochondria, just at a different point in it than glutamine does, so the lining gets another source of energy to heal with, and heals faster.
